All three entries were recorded at head 4a6fc8c431b96c6a71ae3187c6b39d126c1b81c9 while the story is now at HEAD 8d09684be088f99680e7a31cdae7ccab3176aac5, so there is no fresh proof that the must-priority documentation coverage was re-checked on the current story state.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/authority-session-receipt-gate-execution.md:134 and :261 WHY: the document says the receipt-ref artifact must let a consumer answer which gate consumed the receipt, but the example uses gateConsumers=["REVIEW","TEST","DONE"] as a static field on the ref itself. That collapses eligibility and actual consumption into one value and creates an overclaim risk where a ref can appear to have satisfied DONE before any DONE decision consumed it. Fix: split static eligibility from recorded consumption events, or remove gateConsumers from the example until a per-gate consumption schema is defined.
findings.resolvedReason: Changed the receipt-ref example to separate static eligibleGates from per-gate consumptionEvents, removing the static gateConsumers field and the overclaim risk.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/authority-session-receipt-gate-execution.md:331 and :352 present Phase 3/4 as a normal technical rollout for the Lattice CLI, but docs/requirements/decisions/authority-client-role.md:280, :320, :373, and :401 require any CLI authority-client / gate-consumption work to remain deferred behind explicit enforce-mode product approval and the isolated `koala authority enforce` path. WHY: this doc currently lets an implementer read server/runner readiness as sufficient to start ordinary CLI authority-client or gate-integration work, which violates the current thin-client boundary and milestone routing truth source.
findings.resolvedReason: Added hard prerequisites to Phase 3 and Phase 4: explicit enforce-mode product approval, isolated koala authority enforce path, and no ordinary CLI authority-client/gate-consumption rollout based only on server/runner readiness.
